paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “When faced with differing opinions, we should try to reach agreement through friendly discussion and reasonable argument.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“当面对不同意见时，我们应该通过友好讨论和合理论证来达成一致”。您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: You might not know yourself as well as you think. According to a new study, people are 26 accurate judges of only some of their behaviors. While most previous studies on how well people know themselves have been done on long-term personality traits, this new study 27 how well people understand how they are acting from one moment to the next. Researchers asked participants to wear audio recorders that automatically 28 every 9.5 minutes between 7 a.m. and 2 a.m. to record 30 seconds of audio. These participants were then emailed surveys four times a day asking them to 29 how outgoing, agreeable, or conscientious they were during a particular hour of the day. The study used data from 248 participants, all of whom answered questions about their behavior for two 30 weeks and wore the audio device for one of those weeks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 你可能并不像你想象的那样了解自己。一项新的研究表明，人们只能对自己的某些行为做出相对准确的判断。虽然之前大多数关于人们对自己的了解程度的研究都是针对长期人格特征进行的，但这项新研究探讨了人们对自己从一个时刻到下一个时刻的行为方式的理解程度。研究人员要求参与者佩戴录音机，录音机在早上 7 点到凌晨 2 点之间每 9.5 分钟自动启动一次，录制 30 秒的音频。然后，这些参与者每天会收到四次电子邮件调查问卷，要求他们回忆自己在一天中的某个特定时间里有多外向、愉快或认真。该研究使用了 248 名参与者的数据，所有参与者都连续两周回答有关其行为的问题，并在其中一周佩戴音频设备。

paragraphs.sourceText: Six laboratory assistants rated each participant’s audio clips to see how their observations compared with people’s 31 of themselves. The six assistants were generally in agreement with one another about how the people they were observing acted. Further, participants’ ratings of their own behaviors agreed with observers’ for how outgoing and how conscientious they were being. But the agreement between participants and outside observers was much smaller for agreeableness. Some of this 32 could be because the observers used only audio clips, and thus could not read 33 like body language, but there are 34 other explanations, as people should be able to hear when a participant is being kind versus being rude. The weak agreement between how participants thought they were acting and what observers heard could be because people would rather 35 rude behavior.
paragraphs.translationZh: 六名实验室助理对每个参与者的音频片段进行了评分，以了解他们的观察结果与人们对自己的评估有何不同。对于他们所观察的人的行为方式，六位助手大体上达成了一致。此外，参与者对自己行为的评价与观察者对他们的外向和认真程度的评价一致。但参与者和外部观察者之间的一致性要小得多。这种差异的部分原因可能是因为观察者只使用音频剪辑，因此无法读取肢体语言等线索，但可能还有其他解释，因为人们应该能够听到参与者何时是友善的还是粗鲁的。参与者认为自己的行为方式与观察者听到的内容之间的一致性较差，可能是因为人们宁愿否认粗鲁的行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why We Need Tiny Colleges
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么我们需要小型大学

paragraphs.sourceText: A) We’re experiencing the rebirth of smallness. Farmers markets, tiny homes, and brew pubs all exemplify our love of smallness. So do charter schools, coffee shops, and local bookstores. Small is often (but not always) more affordable, healthier, and sustainable, but its finest characteristic, the one that turns charm into love, is that going small allows us to be more fully who we are.
paragraphs.translationZh: A）我们正在经历渺小的重生。农贸市场、小房子和啤酒酒吧都体现了我们对小空间的热爱。特许学校、咖啡馆和当地书店也是如此。小往往（但并非总是）更实惠​​、更健康、更可持续，但它最好的特点，将魅力转化为爱，是小让我们能够更充分地成为我们自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) In higher education the trend is mostly in the opposite direction: Universities with 20,000 or 30,000 students are considered “mid-sized”. The nation’s largest university, Arizona State University, has 80,000 students on campus and aims to enroll another 100,000 students online. At the other end of the spectrum is a handful of colleges that have fewer than a hundred students on campus and no online courses: colleges such as Sterling College, Thomas More College of Liberal Arts, and Deep Springs College. These colleges are so small that they can only be called “tiny.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 在高等教育中，趋势大多相反：拥有 20,000 或 30,000 名学生的大学被视为“中型”大学。美国最大的大学亚利桑那州立大学拥有 80,000 名在校学生，并计划在网上招收另外 100,000 名学生。另一端是少数在校学生不到一百人且没有在线课程的大学：斯特林学院、托马斯莫尔文学院和深泉学院等学院。这些学院规模很小，只能称为“小”。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Tiny colleges focus not just on a young person’s intellect, but on the young person as a whole. Equally important, tiny colleges ask, “How can education contribute to human flourishing and the well-being of the world?” And they shape a college experience to address that question. They replace concerns about institutional growth with attention to the growth of students as fully developed participants in their communities.
paragraphs.translationZh: C）小型学院不仅关注年轻人的智力，而且关注年轻人的整体。同样重要的是，小型大学提出这样的问题：“教育如何为人类繁荣和世界福祉做出贡献？”他们塑造了大学经历来解决这个问题。他们不再关注机构发展，而是关注学生作为社区中充分发展的参与者的成长。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) I’ve had the privilege of teaching at three different institutions of higher learning during my career — a small liberal arts college and two mid-sized public universities. I’ve also been profoundly disappointed in each of these institutions, and in many of my colleagues, especially when it comes to helping students and preparing them for the many responsibilities of adulthood. Administrators focus on the business of running a university, and most faculty focus on their scholarship and teaching their discipline. Little deliberate attention is given to how students mature as individuals and social beings.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 在我的职业生涯中，我有幸在三所不同的高等教育机构任教——一所小型文理学院和两所中型公立大学。我对这些机构以及我的许多同事也深感失望，尤其是在帮助学生并让他们为成年后的许多责任做好准备方面。管理人员专注于管理大学的业务，而大多数教师则专注于他们的学术和学科教学。很少有人刻意关注学生作为个人和社会人如何成熟。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Having just retired from teaching at a public university, I’m now returning to my hometown of Flagstaff, Arizona, to establish a tiny college — Flagstaff College. I’m convinced there’s a need for another type of education, one devoted to helping students come into their own and into this beautiful and troubled world. Young people need an education that will provide them with meaning, hope, courage, and passion, as well as information and skills. Large institutions, I believe, are particularly ill-suited to this type of education.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 我刚刚从一所公立大学的教学中退休，现在回到我的家乡亚利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫，建立一所小型学院——弗拉格斯塔夫学院。我坚信需要另一种类型的教育，致力于帮助学生进入自己的世界，进入这个美丽而充满麻烦的世界。年轻人需要接受能够为他们提供意义、希望、勇气和热情以及信息和技能的教育。我认为大型机构特别不适合这种类型的教育。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) There’s no “best of” list when it comes to tiny colleges, at least not yet. But around the country people are creating new colleges that provide an alternative to small liberal arts colleges, large public universities, and online education.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 对于小型大学来说，还没有“最好”的名单，至少目前还没有。但全国各地的人们正在创建新的学院，为小型文理学院、大型公立大学和在线教育提供替代方案。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) With only 26 students, Deep Springs is the smallest college in the country and, quite likely, the most atypical (非典型的). Located on a working cattle ranch on the California-Nevada border, Deep Springs is a private, residential, two-year college for men, committed to educating students for “a life of service to humanity.” Founded by the electricity tycoon (大亨) L. L. Nunn in 1917, Deep Springs’ “curriculum” revolves around academics, labor, and self-governance. In addition to their courses, students are charged with running the 155-acre ranch and overseeing the functioning of the college. Students chair both the admissions and the curriculum committees.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 深泉学院只有 26 名学生，是全国最小的学院，而且很可能是最非典型的学院。深泉学院位于加利福尼亚州和内华达州边境的一个正在运营的牧场上，是一所私立、两年制住宿男子学院，致力于教育学生“为人类服务”。 Deep Springs 由电力大亨 L. L. Nunn 于 1917 年创立，其“课程”围绕学术、劳工和自治展开。除了课程之外，学生还负责管理 155 英亩的牧场并监督学院的运作。学生担任招生委员会和课程委员会的主席。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) “Living in close community with one’s teachers and fellow students, and being forced to take on adult responsibilities, makes for one’s growth as a person,” says William Hunt, who graduated last year. “To exist for very long in a community like that, you have to get over the question of whether you’re sufficiently talented or principled and get started worrying about how you can stretch yourself and your peers, how much you can manage to learn with them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H）“与老师和同学生活在紧密的社区中，被迫承担成人的责任，有助于一个人的成长，”去年毕业的威廉·亨特说。 “要想在这样的社区中生存很长时间，你必须克服自己是否足够有才华或有原则的问题，并开始担心如何才能拓展自己和同事，以及如何能够与他们一起学习。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Sterling College, in Craftsbury Common, Vermont, is also very small — fewer than 100 students. Unlike Deep Springs, Sterling focuses its curriculum on environmental and social justice issues, but like Deep Springs it places a high value on personal responsibility and manual labor. According to its catalog, a college education at Sterling combines “rigorous academics, roll-up-your-sleeves challenges, and good old hard work.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 斯特林学院 (Sterling College) 位于佛蒙特州 Craftsbury Common，规模也很小，学生人数不到 100 名。与 Deep Springs 不同，Sterling 的课程重点关注环境和社会正义问题，但与 Deep Springs 一样，它也高度重视个人责任和体力劳动。根据其目录，斯特林大学的大学教育结合了“严谨的学术、卷起袖子迎接挑战和良好的辛勤工作”。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The average tuition at a small liberal-arts college is $30,000 to $40,000 a year, not including the cost of living on campus, as compared to $8,000 to $10,000 a year for tuition alone at a public university. Of the tiny colleges, only Deep Springs doesn’t charge tuition or room and board; students pay only for books and the cost of traveling to and from college. If tiny schools are to become a player on the higher education scene, they will need to find a way to be truly affordable.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 小型文理学院的平均学费为每年 30,000 至 40,000 美元，不包括校园生活费用，而公立大学的学费每年为 8,000 至 10,000 美元。在小型学院中，只有 Deep Springs 不收取学费或食宿费。学生只需支付书本费和往返大学的交通费用。如果小型学校要成为高等教育领域的一员，他们将需要找到一种真正负担得起的方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Doing so may not be that difficult so long as they do not pattern themselves too closely on existing norms. We’ve come to believe that a good college should have many academic programs and excellent facilities, posh (豪华的) dorms, an array of athletic programs, and a world-class student activity center. Imagine a good college without a climbing wall! We also have accepted the idea that college presidents, and their many vice-presidents, should be paid like their counterparts in the business world and that higher education requires an elaborate, up-to-date technology infrastructure. All of this drives up the cost of education.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 只要他们不过度遵循现有规范，这样做可能并不困难。我们开始相信，一所好的大学应该拥有许多学术课程和优良的设施、豪华的宿舍、一系列的体育项目以及世界一流的学生活动中心。想象一下，一所没有攀岩墙的好大学！我们还接受了这样的观点，即大学校长及其众多副校长的薪酬应与商界同行相同，并且高等教育需要复杂的、最新的技术基础设施。所有这些都推高了教育成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) The “trick” to making tiny colleges affordable, if that’s the right word, is simplicity. At its core, education is a human-to-human interaction. Reflecting on his own college education, President Garfield once commented that an ideal college would consist of nothing more than the legendary teacher Mark Hopkins on one end of a log and a student on the other. The economics of a tiny college, in other words, might be similar to that of a tiny house. Because it is small, a tiny house costs less to build and less to furnish, insure, and maintain. But the economic benefits of a small house don’t end there. Tiny homes discourage homeowners from buying stuff that they really don’t need, because there’s no place to put it.
paragraphs.translationZh: L）让小型大学负担得起的“技巧”（如果这个词合适的话）就是简单。教育的核心是人与人之间的互动。加菲尔德总统在反思自己的大学教育时曾评论说，一所理想的大学只不过是一根木头的一端是传奇教师马克霍普金斯，另一端是一名学生。换句话说，一所小型大学的经济效益可能类似于一栋小房子的经济效益。因为小房子很小，所以建造成本较低，家具、保险和维护成本也较低。但小房子的经济效益还不止于此。小房子会阻止房主购买他们真正不需要的东西，因为没有地方放。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) I’m a late convert to the idea of tiny colleges, and I fully understand the need for many diverse types of educational institutions. Academic research and job training are important, but tiny colleges aren’t suited for either. The educational needs of a complex society are themselves complex, and no single model can meet all of these needs. But I’m now convinced there’s an educational need that’s now going almost completely unmet: namely, the need to help young people transition into adulthood. Tiny colleges can do this better than any other type of educational institution.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 我是一个较晚才接受小型大学理念的人，我完全理解对多种不同类型教育机构的需求。学术研究和职业培训很重要，但小型大学都不适合。复杂社会的教育需求本身也是复杂的，没有一种模式能够满足所有这些需求。但我现在确信有一种教育需求现在几乎完全没有得到满足：即帮助年轻人过渡到成年的需要。小型学院比任何其他类型的教育机构都能更好地做到这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The ultimate justification for a tiny college is the conviction that each of us comes into our full humanity by close interaction with those who know and care for us, and that one of the basic purposes of higher education is social. Although we give lip service to the idea that a college education will make us better people, when all’s said and done, we think of higher education primarily in economic terms. We’ve come to think of higher education as a means to make a living rather than make a life. We’ve also come to see higher education as a private good rather than a public one. Tiny colleges are not the answer to all of our educational requirements, but they’re an answer to one of our most basic educational necessities: the need to produce thoughtful, engaged, and compassionate human beings.
paragraphs.translationZh: N）一所小型大学的最终理由是相信我们每个人都通过与那些了解和关心我们的人密切互动而获得完整的人性，并且高等教育的基本目的之一是社会性。尽管我们口头上承认大学教育将使我们成为更好的人，但归根结底，我们主要从经济角度考虑高等教育。我们已经开始将高等教育视为谋生手段，而不是谋生的手段。我们也开始将高等教育视为一种私人物品而不是公共物品。小型大学并不能满足我们所有的教育要求，但它们可以满足我们最基本的教育需求之一：培养有思想、投入和富有同情心的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. One tiny American college situated on a cattle farm is devoted to educating students to serve mankind throughout their lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 位于养牛场的一所小型美国大学致力于教育学生终其一生为人类服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Much to the author’s disappointment, the three institutions of higher learning where she taught largely ignore students’ growth as social beings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 令作者非常失望的是，她任教的三所高等教育机构基本上忽视了学生作为社会人的成长。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Tiny colleges must be made affordable in order to play a role in higher education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 小型学院必须负担得起才能在高等教育中发挥作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. According to a recent graduate from a tiny college, living together with faculty and fellow students is conducive to a student’s growth as a person.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 据一所小型大学的应届毕业生称，与教师和同学住在一起有利于学生的成长。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Rather than going small, most American universities are trying to go big.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 大多数美国大学都在尝试做大，而不是做小。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. In a certain tiny college, rigorous academic work and traditional manual labor are integrated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41.在一所小学院里，严谨的学术工作和传统的体力劳动融为一体。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Tiny colleges focus on educating students to become well-rounded citizens instead of seeking their own expansion.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 小型学院专注于教育学生成为全面发展的公民，而不是寻求自身的扩张。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The essence of education lies in the interaction between people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 教育的本质在于人与人之间的互动。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you’re someone who has turned to snacking on junk food more in the pandemic (大流行病）， you’re not alone. Investigative reporter Michael Moss says processed food is engineered to hook you, not unlike alcohol, cigarettes, or other harmful substances. His 2013 book, Salt Sugar Fat, explored food companies’ aggressive marketing of those products and their impact on our health. In his new book, Hooked, Moss updates the food giants’ efforts to keep us eating what they serve, and how they’re responding to complaints from consumers and health advocates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你是在大流行病中更多地吃垃圾食品的人，那么你并不孤单。调查记者迈克尔·莫斯说，加工食品的设计就是为了让你着迷，就像酒精、香烟或其他有害物质一样。他在 2013 年出版的书《盐糖脂肪》探讨了食品公司对这些产品的积极营销及其对我们健康的影响。在他的新书《上瘾》中，莫斯更新了食品巨头为让我们吃他们所提供的食物所做的努力，以及他们如何回应消费者和健康倡导者的投诉。

paragraphs.sourceText: Processed food is inexpensive, it’s legal, and it’s everywhere. Companies’ advertising is cueing us to remember those products and we want those products constantly. So the food environment is one of those key things that makes food even more problematic for so many people. Memory, nostalgia (怀旧) in particular, plays a big role in the foods we crave. Soda companies discovered that if they put a soda in the hands of a child when they’re at a ball game with their parents, that soda will forever be associated with that joyous moment. Later in life, when that child wants to experience a joyous moment, they’re going to think of soda. Many people seek comfort in the snacks they remember from childhood.
paragraphs.translationZh: 加工食品价格便宜、合法，而且无处不在。公司的广告正在暗示我们记住这些产品，并且我们不断地想要这些产品。因此，食品环境是导致许多人的食品问题更加严重的关键因素之一。记忆，尤其是怀旧，在我们渴望的食物中发挥着重要作用。汽水公司发现，如果他们在孩子与父母一起打球时将汽水放在孩子手中，那么汽水将永远与那个欢乐的时刻联系在一起。在以后的生活中，当孩子想要体验快乐的时刻时，他们会想到苏打水。许多人从童年记忆中的零食中寻求安慰。

paragraphs.sourceText: Moss examines the way companies capitalize on our memories, cravings and brain chemistry to keep us snacking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 莫斯研究了公司如何利用我们的记忆、渴望和大脑化学物质来让我们吃零食。

paragraphs.sourceText: One of the reasons I came to think that some of these food products are even more powerful, more troublesome than drugs can be is memory. What we eat is all about memory. And we begin forming memories for food at a really early age. And we keep those memories for a lifetime. Knowing this, the food industry spends lots of time trying to shape the memories that we have for their products. One of the features of addiction that scientists studying drug addiction discovered back in the 1990s was that the faster a substance hits the brain, the more apt we are as a result to act impulsively. There’s nothing faster than food in its ability to hit the brain. For Moss, this puts the notion of “fast food” in an entirely new light as this isn’t limited to fast food chains — almost 90% of food products in grocery stores are processed foods. Everything in the industry is about speed, from manufacturing to packaging.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我开始认为这些食品比药物更强大、更麻烦的原因之一是记忆。我们吃的东西都是关于记忆的。我们很小的时候就开始形成对食物的记忆。我们会终生保留这些记忆。知道这一点后，食品行业花费了大量时间试图塑造我们对其产品的记忆。研究毒瘾的科学家早在 20 世纪 90 年代就发现了毒瘾的特征之一，那就是物质到达大脑的速度越快，我们就越容易做出冲动的行为。没有什么比食物能够更快地冲击大脑了。对于莫斯来说，这让“快餐”的概念焕然一新，因为这不仅限于快餐连锁店——杂货店里几乎 90% 的食品都是加工食品。从制造到包装，该行业的一切都与速度有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: Overall, Moss outlines the industry’s dependence on making their products inexpensive, super delicious, and incredibly convenient for consumers. Now that more and more people care about what they put in their bodies and are wanting to eat healthier, these companies are finding it really difficult to meet that new demand because of their own addiction to making these convenience foods.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总体而言，莫斯概述了该行业对让产品价格低廉、超级美味且对消费者来说极其方便的依赖。现在，越来越多的人关心自己吃的东西，并希望吃得更健康，这些公司发现很难满足这种新的需求，因为他们自己对制作这些方便食品上瘾。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Chimpanzees (黑猩猩), human beings’ closest animal relatives, share up to 98% of our genes. Yet humans and chimpanzees lead very different lives. Fewer than 300,000 wild chimpanzees live in a few forested corners of Africa today, while humans have colonized every corner of the globe. At more than 7 billion, human population dwarfs that of nearly all other mammals — despite our physical weaknesses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 黑猩猩是人类最亲近的动物近亲，与我们有高达 98% 的基因相同。然而人类和黑猩猩的生活却截然不同。如今，只有不到 30 万只野生黑猩猩生活在非洲的几个森林角落，而人类却已经占领了全球每个角落。尽管我们的体质较弱，但人类人口超过 70 亿，使几乎所有其他哺乳动物相形见绌。

paragraphs.sourceText: What could account for our species’ incredible evolutionary successes?
paragraphs.translationZh: 什么可以解释我们物种令人难以置信的进化成功？

paragraphs.sourceText: One obvious answer is our big brains. It could be that our raw intelligence gave us an unprecedented ability to think outside the box, innovating solutions to thorny problems as people migrated across the globe.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个明显的答案是我们的大大脑。可能是我们的原始智力赋予了我们前所未有的跳出框框思考的能力，为人们在全球迁徙时遇到的棘手问题提供创新的解决方案。

paragraphs.sourceText: But a growing number of cognitive scientists and anthropologists (人类学家) are rejecting that explanation. They think that, rather than making our living as innovators, we survive and thrive precisely because we don’t think for ourselves. Instead, people cope with challenging climates and ecological contexts by carefully copying others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但越来越多的认知科学家和人类学家拒绝这种解释。他们认为，我们之所以生存和繁荣，不是因为我们以创新者的身份谋生，而是因为我们不独立思考。相反，人们通过仔细模仿他人来应对具有挑战性的气候和生态环境。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a famous study, psychologists Victoria Horner and Andrew Whiten showed two groups of test subjects — children and chimpanzees — a mechanical box with a treat inside. In one condition, the box was opaque, while in the other it was transparent. The experimenters demonstrated how to open the box to retrieve the treat, but they also included the irrelevant step of tapping on the box with a stick.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一项著名的研究中，心理学家维多利亚·霍纳和安德鲁·怀特恩向两组测试对象（儿童和黑猩猩）展示了一个机械盒子，里面有零食。在一种情况下，盒子是不透明的，而在另一种情况下，盒子是透明的。实验者演示了如何打开盒子来取出零食，但他们也包括了用棍子敲击盒子的不相关步骤。

paragraphs.sourceText: Oddly, the children carefully copied all the steps to open the box, even when they could see that the stick had no practical effect. That is, they copied irrationally: Instead of doing only what was necessary to get their reward, children slavishly imitated every action they’d witnessed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 奇怪的是，孩子们还是小心翼翼地复制了打开盒子的所有步骤，即使他们看到棍子没有任何实际作用。也就是说，他们非理性地模仿：孩子们不是只做获得奖励所必需的事情，而是盲目地模仿他们所目睹的每一个动作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course, that study only included three- and four-year-olds. But additional research has shown that older children and adults are even more likely to mindlessly copy others’ actions, and infants are less likely to over-imitate — that is, to precisely copy even impractical actions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，这项研究只包括三岁和四岁的孩子。但更多的研究表明，年龄较大的儿童和成人更有可能无意识地模仿他人的行为，而婴儿则不太可能过度模仿——也就是说，精确地模仿甚至不切实际的行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: By contrast, chimpanzees in the study only over-imitated in the opaque condition. In the transparent condition — where they saw that the stick was mechanically useless — they ignored that step entirely. Other research has since supported these findings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相比之下，研究中的黑猩猩只是在不透明的条件下过度模仿。在透明条件下——他们看到棍子在机械上毫无用处——他们完全忽略了这一步。此后其他研究也支持了这些发现。

paragraphs.sourceText: When it comes to copying, chimpanzees are more rational than human children or adults.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在模仿方面，黑猩猩比人类儿童或成人更加理性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Where does the seemingly irrational human preference for over-imitation come from? Anthropologist Joseph Henrich points out that people around the world rely on technologies that are often so complex that no one can learn them rationally. Instead, people must learn them step by step, trusting in the wisdom of more experienced elders and peers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人类看似非理性的过度模仿偏好从何而来？人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇指出，世界各地的人们所依赖的技术往往非常复杂，以至于没有人能够理性地学习它们。相反，人们必须一步一步地学习它们，相信更有经验的长辈和同龄人的智慧。

paragraphs.sourceText: So the next time you hear someone arguing passionately that everyone should embrace nonconformity and avoid imitating others, you might laugh a little bit. We’re not chimpanzees, after all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，下次当你听到有人热情地争论每个人都应该接受不墨守成规、避免模仿他人时，你可能会笑一笑。毕竟我们不是黑猩猩。

paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 什么可以解释人类几乎是所有哺乳动物中数量最多的？
